skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-meta-poas-bidding
skill.description: Set up Meta Ads bidding on WooCommerce order profit instead of revenue with Product Metrics and the Meta Conversions API. Check costs and consent, verify a test event, and choose a starting target based on profit on ad spend.
skill.summary: Guide WooCommerce merchants through profit-based bidding in Meta Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most scanner hits are Markdown literals, public links, or routine setup guidance; the remote MCP execution path and unpinned installer warrant review. The workflow can expose credentials, act without explicit account or write approval, and enable broader conversion sharing than the profit setup suggests. The fallback to live instructions also creates a trust risk; no evidence of malicious intent or an audit override was found.

remediation.issue: The assistant is told to request API credentials and pass them directly to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to enter Meta tokens in the Product Metrics app or a dedicated secret input. Remove instructions to collect raw credentials in chat or pass them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not require explicit approval for the account scope or authenticated setup writes.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace, store, and destination before reading order records. Show proposed changes and obtain approval before writes. Restrict MCP operations to an allowlist for this workflow.

remediation.issue: Adding a Meta destination enables more data sharing than a profit-only setup implies.
remediation.suggestion: Show the event types, customer fields, signed margins, and consent requirements before enabling live sending. Confirm the destination and obtain approval for the full data scope.

remediation.issue: Missing references cause the agent to follow mutable web documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle versioned references with every distribution. Treat remote documentation as background information, not as authority to make changes or handle credentials.

remediation.issue: The optional installation command uses an unpinned package and skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and skill revision, and require user approval before running an installer.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant Collection of API Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits the assistant to request raw API secrets and pass them to a command. The Meta guide both recommends app entry and requires the assistant to ask for the token. Without a dedicated secret input, credentials could enter chat history or tool traces.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files explicitly authorize asking for the token. The reviewed text does not specify a secure assistant input that keeps it out of conversation and tool records.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Approval for Account Scope and Setup Writes
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs use of Product Metrics even when the merchant does not name it. It takes account identifiers from tool results and permits setup writes and order lookups without requiring confirmation of the intended account or action.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rules reserve bidding changes and deletes for the user, but do not require approval for other writes or confirmation before reading orders. Wrong-account access is possible when multiple accounts are available.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Setup Shares More Than Order Profit
semantic_findings.description: The Meta setup instructs the merchant to leave event sending enabled. Besides profit values, the destination can receive other events, matching data, and signed losses. The step does not ask the merchant to review that full scope before enabling delivery.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The enablement step and expanded payload are documented. The references describe consent requirements, so this is a disclosure and approval gap, not evidence of a consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Live Documentation Can Replace Reviewed Instructions
semantic_findings.description: If local references are missing, the agent is directed to fetch live Markdown and use it as the setup procedure. Changes to that content could influence later credential handling or API actions without changing the audited skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly substitutes unpinned vendor pages for bundled references. No evidence of malicious remote content was found.

content.user_title: Set Up Profit Bidding for WooCommerce in Meta Ads
content.value_statement: A campaign can meet its revenue target while losing money after product costs, fees, and shipping. Use Product Metrics to send order profit to Meta and start bidding against a profit target.
actual_capabilities: Check connection and setup status through the Product Metrics CLI or MCP when available.
Guide merchants through WooCommerce plugin setup, paid order statuses, consent settings, and the Meta destination.
Identify cost sources for products, payment fees, and shipping, and explain what to check when profit is missing.
Guide merchants through test order verification and creation of a Meta custom conversion for PMOrderProfit.
Suggest an initial profit target from current profit on ad spend and explain how it differs from a revenue target.
Explain how to retain revenue-based bidding with the standard Purchase event.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, administrator access to WordPress, and access to the Meta pixel.
The merchant creates the custom conversion and changes ad set optimization in Meta.
Profit events require known costs and both marketing and analytics consent.
Meta does not revise events for later refunds. The skill does not cover other ad channels or customer lifetime value bidding.

use_cases.title: Review a Campaign That Meets Its Revenue Goal
use_cases.description: Check whether product costs, payment fees, and shipping leave enough contribution profit to cover ad spend.

use_cases.title: Pilot Profit-Based Bidding
use_cases.description: Choose one Meta ad set, verify its profit event, and set an initial goal based on current profit on ad spend.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Profit Events
use_cases.description: Check cost sources, consent settings, and test mode when Meta receives revenue events but no profit events.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Revenue and Profit Bidding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain ROAS and POAS using an order that earns $100 in revenue and $30 in contribution profit before $20 in ad spend.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn how order costs change the bidding target.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: List the WooCommerce, Product Metrics, and Meta prerequisites for profit bidding. Point out where I enter tokens myself. Make no account changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Check access and configuration before connecting a store.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Missing Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Meta shows Purchase but not PMOrderProfit for my test order. Give me a checklist for costs, consent, and test events. Ask for no secrets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Troubleshoot profit event delivery before selecting a conversion.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a One-Ad-Set Pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: My ad set has a revenue ROAS of 4.2 and a POAS of 1.5. Propose a profit goal and list what I should verify in Events Manager before switching. Make no changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a controlled move from revenue to profit bidding.

output_examples.input: My ad set has a current POAS of 1.5. What starting target should I use?
output_examples.output: Start at 150% on the profit event for one ad set. At that ratio, $1.50 in tracked contribution profit covers $1.00 in ad spend and leaves $0.50. Review results after a few weeks.

output_examples.input: My test order appears as Purchase, but the profit conversion is missing.
output: Confirm that the test order has all required costs and that analytics and marketing consent were granted.
Place another test order if you corrected costs or consent. Check for PMOrderProfit in Meta Events Manager.
Once the event arrives, create the custom conversion and clear the test event code before checking live delivery.

best_practices: Verify the intended store and pixel, review what data will be sent, and enter tokens directly in the approved app or plugin.
Verify a consented test order with complete costs, then clear the test event code before relying on reporting.
Start with one ad set and base the profit target on its current POAS.
anti_patterns: Copying a revenue target directly to a profit event.
Pasting API credentials or one-time setup tokens into an assistant conversation.
Treating a test event as proof that live reporting is active.

faq.question: What is the difference between POAS and ROAS?
faq.answer: POAS divides contribution profit by ad spend. ROAS divides revenue by ad spend.

faq.question: Which Meta event should I use?
faq.answer: For profit bidding, use a custom conversion based on PMOrderProfit with the purpose set to ORDER_PROFIT. For revenue bidding, use Purchase.

faq.question: What happens when costs are missing or an order loses money?
faq.answer: An order with incomplete costs can still send a revenue event, but not a profit event. For a loss, Meta receives zero as the conversion value and the signed loss separately.

faq.question: What consent does the profit event require?
faq.answer: PMOrderProfit requires both marketing and analytics consent. The guide lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano as supported banners.

faq.question: Can the assistant switch the ad set for me?
faq.answer: No. You create the custom conversion in Meta Events Manager and select it as the ad set's optimization event.

faq.question: Will Meta receive past orders or later refund updates?
faq.answer: Past orders are not imported into Meta. Later refunds do not revise events that Meta has already received.
